Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET-09 - unverified image-only reading
Exposure: no proposed identification or prior reading was in my context. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (I listed the packet directory and checked image pixel sizes with sips to tell overviews from tiles; did not open packet.json).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of first face/set)
- image-001 is an overview of a black board holding ~12 separate small paper(?)/parchment fragments plus a colour checker and a cm scale (right edge, ~38 cm). The fragments are offcuts (binding strips/pieces), not a single leaf.
- Top row: two upright fragments (left), two landscape fragments (right). Middle row: two landscape fragments (centre-right), one bearing a large red/blue-flourished initial "N" with a red rubric line in display script to its right. Bottom row: one landscape fragment (left of centre), then four upright fragments; one upright (4th from left in bottom row) shows very dense small text in two narrow columns with no red - a different, more cursive/denser hand (possibly a gloss or different MS).
- Most fragments show a single text column of a small gothic book hand in brown ink, with red paragraph marks / red strokes (line-fillers or rubricated capital strokes) at many line starts. Some show a vertical fold/crease or a ruled column boundary. Pencil shelfmark-style notes "Stams STA Frg. 32-..." visible on several pieces (modern).
- One bottom-row fragment has a drawn circle (compass-drawn) faintly visible - possibly a diagram, or show-through.
- Text orientation: on several pieces the text runs upright; on some upright-format pieces the text lines run horizontally across a narrow width (cut column).
- Tiles image-002..013 are presumably native-resolution tiles of this overview in a 4x3 grid (002-005 top, 006-009 middle, 010-013 bottom), overlapping.


=== image-002 (top-left tile: fragment A = upright piece with pencil "STA, Frg. 30.11r"(?) and left part of fragment B) ===
Observations: paper(?) or very abraded parchment, ink badly faded and rubbed, with show-through. Fragment A appears to carry two text columns (left column x~80-700, right column x~750-1050, right column cut at the fragment edge). Red ink is used as horizontal underlining strokes under words (several per column), i.e. red underlining of selected words (likely lemmata/citations; interpretation tentative). Small gothic textualis/semi-cursive hand with frequent abbreviations. Fragment A is largely illegible at this resolution even with contrast enhancement; I selected fragment B (right edge, x~1340-1790) as the most legible span.
